title: spec(extension): Settlement Attestation Receipt (SAR)
body:
## Summary

Proposes a new x402 extension — **Settlement Attestation Receipt (SAR)** — that binds payment settlement to resource delivery in a single verifiable artifact.

### The gap this addresses

x402 solves how agents pay. The `offer-receipt` extension proves a server acknowledged payment. But neither artifact proves that **what was delivered matches what was agreed upon**. In agent-to-agent commerce, this gap matters: the paying agent needs a machine-verifiable proof it can present to its principal.

A SAR binds three facts into one signed object:
1. **Payment settled** — transaction hash and network
2. **Resource delivered** — content hash of the response body
3. **Terms matched** — digest linking back to the signed offer

### Design choices

- **Composes with `offer-receipt`**, does not replace it. The `offerDigest` field creates a cryptographic chain: terms → payment → delivery.
- **Content hash, not content**: proves integrity without revealing the response to third-party verifiers (privacy-preserving).
- **Same signature formats** (EIP-712 / JWS) and conventions as `offer-receipt` for implementer consistency.
- **No new actor responsibilities**: the facilitator is not involved. The resource server generates, the client verifies.

### Use cases

- Agent accountability (orchestrator verifies sub-agent delivery)
- Automated SLA enforcement (compare `deliveredAt` against offer `validUntil`)
- Compliance audit trails
- Dispute resolution with content integrity proof

## Test plan

- [ ] Review spec structure against existing extension conventions
- [ ] Verify EIP-712 type definition consistency with `offer-receipt`
- [ ] Confirm no conflicts with `payment-identifier` or other extensions

title: specs(exact/evm): state the EIP-712 domain mapping for the eip3009 method
body:
`scheme_exact_evm.md` Phase 2 step 1 says to "verify the signature is valid and recovers to the `authorization.from` address". The types needed to do that are normative — `x402-specification-v2.md` §6.1.1 defines `TransferWithAuthorization` — but the **domain** that completes the EIP-712 digest is never named in the spec text:

- `verifyingContract` does not appear in **any** normative `.md` in this repository;
- `extra.name` and `extra.version`, which the domain needs, occur **only inside the JSON examples** — never described in prose, never typed.

An implementer gets there by knowing EIP-3009 and inferring the mapping. That inference is correct and most people will make it. The cost is paid by the one who doesn't: a wrong domain produces no typed error, it produces a signature that recovers to a different address, which step 1 can only report as "invalid signature". Same failure mode being discussed for `offerDigest` in #46.

**Scope: editorial, not a security defect.** Nothing here is exploitable, and x402 cannot define `name`/`version` normatively — they belong to the token instance, not to the protocol. What was missing is the *mapping*: which payment fields populate which domain parameters. Four rows.

### The example already in the document is cryptographically genuine

This is what makes the table checkable rather than asserted. The signature in `scheme_exact_evm.md` **verifies**: recovering it under the mapping proposed here yields exactly `authorization.from` (`0x857b06519E91e3A54538791bDbb0E22373e36b66`). Whoever wrote that example signed it for real, and the four values in the table are the ones actually used.

I checked this with a clean-room reader written from the normative `.md` files only — never the Go/TypeScript/Python reference implementations — with Keccak-256 and secp256k1 implemented from scratch in the Python standard library. The bench is validated before it measures: Keccak against three published values, EIP-712 against the three digests published in EIP-712 itself for the canonical `Mail` example (`domainSeparator f2cee375…`, `hashStruct c52c0ee5…`, `signingDigest be609aee…`), and secp256k1 against a non-circular signing control.

### Offer, if useful

That example could become `specs/vectors/exact_evm_eip3009.json` — the repository's first conformance vector. There are five official implementations (typescript, python, go, java, contracts) and nine `exact` variants, with no shared byte-level oracle today: every implementation currently verifies itself. I can prepare it, with declared accept/reject verdicts and a runner, if the maintainers want it. Happy to share the clean-room reader either way.

I would have opened this as an issue per `specs/CONTRIBUTING.md` ("open a GitHub issue or discussion"), but both are disabled here — possibly worth a line in that guide.

- `extra.name` and `extra.version`, which the domain needs, occur **only inside the JSON examples** — never described in prose, never typed.

## What

Adds **Synergy** to the ecosystem page under *Services/Endpoints*, per the README's "Adding Your Project to the Ecosystem" steps:

- `typescript/site/app/ecosystem/partners-data/synergy/metadata.json`
- `typescript/site/public/logos/synergy.svg` (512x512)

## About the project

[exo-trust.com](https://exo-trust.com) operates Synergy, a live pay-per-call AI utility gateway for agents, run end-to-end autonomously. 13 production specialists are sold over x402 and settled in USDC on **Base mainnet** (eip155:8453) via the Coinbase CDP facilitator - no accounts, no API keys. Specialist families include translation, text extraction, code explanation, SEC EDGAR financials, sanctions screening (OFAC), EU VAT/VIES and GLEIF LEI lookups, clinical-trial diligence and more, priced $0.002-$2.00 per call.

Machine-readable surfaces, all live on mainnet:
- Catalogue: `https://api.exo-trust.com/discovery` (13 resources, also in the Bazaar)
- OpenAPI: `https://api.exo-trust.com/openapi.json`
- `/.well-known/x402` and `/llms.txt` endpoints
- MCP endpoint (`/mcp`, streamable HTTP) registered as `com.exo-trust/synergy` on the official MCP registry

The gateway answers unpaid requests with a `402 Payment Required` challenge carrying the exact USDC amount and `payTo` address; agents settle via the facilitator and retry with the proof header.
